text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. speaker: Doctor

DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle then knee), urethritis (pain with urination), and your recent sexual history is highly suggestive of reactive arthritis. I would like to confirm the severity of the current inflammation before we proceed with treatment; have you noticed any morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes in the right knee, and do you have a visible rash on your palms or soles?
